body:
Hello, and thank you for the report.

It appears there's a misunderstanding about how the [`partial`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/programming-guide/classes-and-structs/partial-classes-and-methods) keyword works. The `partial` keyword allows you to split a single class definition across multiple files within the **same assembly**. It's a compile-time feature to help organize large classes, it's not related to cross-assembly type resolution.

The problem you're encountering is not related to `partial` classes themselves since, when Godot loads the assembly, the `partial` keyword no longer applies. The real issue is that Godot doesn't automatically register classes defined in assemblies other than the main assembly.

Godot _registers_ your classes by calling the `LookupScriptsInAssembly` method for the main assembly, so it only registers the classes defined in that assembly. At the moment, using scripts from external assemblies is considered unsupported.

It may be possible to work around this limitation by manually calling the `LookupScriptsInAssembly` method as described in the issues you linked, but it has some caveats so **I don't recommend it**. Keep in mind that `LookupScriptsInAssembly` (as most everything else in the `Godot.Bridge` namespace) is not meant to be used by users, it's considered internal API and may be removed in the future.

The issues you linked already track the same problem, so I'll be closing this one to consolidate the discussion in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/75352. Thanks for the report nonetheless.
